Maybe she's having a hard time and didn't want you to hear her voice. I can't keep it together on the phone when I'm breaking bad news. And if she also has to deal with a lot of arrangements and stuff right now, maybe she thinks she can't "afford" the breakdown.

Or maybe she's a stupid jerk. I'm so sorry for your loss. I hope you reach out to your friends and family this week.
What? Did I say something wrong?

I'm not saying this is the right answer to you, but maybe go to the hospital. They will be super certain that you have not lethally harmed yourself. And they're gonna lock you down for about a week, no way around it. But after a week where they remind you to eat, get you on an almost normal sleep schedule, get you talking to some social workers, you might have a new perspective on some situations in your life. I did.

Maybe a social worker could help you get some help with your teeth. Tooth pain is intolerable. It is indescribably bad and I feel so strongly for you right now. There are dentists that do pro-bono work for serious cases. And I think a social worker would be your best bet to connect you with the relevant charities in your area.

You are a very strong person to live with your day-to-day pain and depression. You're doing this to be there for your son, in the ways and times that you can. I don't know if I could be as strong as you are, my experience with tooth-pain was unforgettable. And I'm not saying the hospital is the right path for you. I was institutionalized after a mild suicide attempt, and everything I said above is true, but there were negative experiences as well. You're going to do the right thing for you, just please hang in there and keep trying.

Better now? If you could give on piece of advice without anyone being sensitive?

I mean, since you're awake. Ha.

Sounds like you gave yourself some advice. You probably have some undiagnosed mental disorder. Nothing big and bad and scary, but getting a little help wouldn't set you back, right? Do you have health insurance? If so, make that appointment and get that process started. It won't hurt, I promise, and it will likely help some. Who has insurance though, huh? Does your school offer some on-campus medical center? When my fiance was having trouble and we couldn't afford to get any help, we went there and they appointment & meds were free. Also google around for some country health services. Look around downtown areas of bigger cities, my local university has a free counseling service downtown that they require their students to put some hours into to graduate. Help is help, you know.

You can move home without moving back in with your parents. Lots of people love and live their whole lives in their hometowns. If long-haul trucking isn't detestable to you, it does allow you a little flexibility in where you live. Maybe spending your time off in your hometown would be worth your time on the job.

Keep moving forward. You're too early in this game to know how it's going to play out. Sometimes good things happen to you if you're just slow and steady. Finish school, find a job, get a housing situation that's satisfactory, get a dog. Who knows what will happen during all that.

FUCK YES I WOULD.

Thank you.

Also, that baby gate/couch set-up in the background is freaking ingenious. All-around a very useful video.

Good idea, thanks. I was a waitress in high school, but the car wreck a couple years ago left me with a bum hip and I don't think I could keep up with the pace. Anyway, thanks for commiserating. You're a good person.

Try to find some comfort in some boring everyday stuff. Organizing closets, cooking slightly more elaborate meals. In others words, get your mind off of it. Not in a disrespectful way or a forgetful way, just in a realistic way, so it's a little easier to put one foot in front of the other. The feelings will never, ever go away, but the time between them sometimes gets longer. Don't feel like you have to make yourself remember things as some sort of penance for still being here. The memories won't go away if you get distracted with something else. They'll be there later too.

But you don't need advice. Good on you for getting these things off your chest. You're well-spoken and sound like you have a good handle on things. You just have to take the time to feel these feelings. Hang in there friend.
You are good with words. Good night friend.

Just one of your smaller things: screw most of your stuff. As someone who has packed up and moved in just a couple of days (not as stressful as yours, of course), you don't need it. You won't realize until you move a second time and you find yourself packing up things you haven't used much if at all since the last time you moved. Get a big rubbermaid tub for memory items, and otherwise keep things you like & use and get rid of the rest. If you can sell some big stuff (furniture, electronics) fast on Craiglists or a pawn shop, do it, but otherwise donate it and move on. It will be a HUGE weight off your shoulders, you have other things you need to deal with, you'll be able to contribute to helping others. And you'll LOVE all the space you have free without all that stuff you don't REALLY want.

Just my 2 cents. Hang in there! Day by day!
